en.headline: Competition watchdog searches 11 sites over school VR bids
en.dek: The Competition Commission said Thursday's Lens operation targeted alleged bid-rigging on virtual-reality contracts worth about 10 million dollars.
body: The Competition Commission said it searched 11 premises on Thursday under court warrants, in an operation codenamed Lens, over alleged bid-rigging on contracts to supply virtual-reality systems to schools and non-profit organisations.

The watchdog said the premises included offices of several information-technology service and equipment suppliers, other firms involved, and the homes of several suspects. It said the firms were accused of bid-rigging, price-fixing, market-sharing and exchanging competitively sensitive information when quoting for virtual-reality equipment and software installation.

The commission said it had received complaints that suppliers prepared tender documents for other firms so those bids could act as cover. It put the contracts involved at about 10 million dollars, and said the suspected conduct could reduce choice and raise costs for schools and non-profit bodies, affecting the use of public resources.

The searches were disclosed on Friday. The commission has not said that anyone has been charged. Under the Competition Ordinance, a contravention of the first conduct rule is a matter for the commission to investigate and, where it decides to proceed, for the Competition Tribunal.

zh.headline: 競委會「銳鏡」行動搜查11處所 涉學校VR報價圍標
zh.dek: 競委會周五公布，周四持法庭手令搜查資訊科技供應商辦公室及住所，涉案合約約1000萬元。
body: 競爭事務委員會周五公布，周四展開代號「銳鏡」的執法行動，根據法庭手令搜查11個處所，調查向學校及非牟利機構提供虛擬實境設備及軟件安裝報價時的懷疑圍標。
競委會表示，搜查地點包括多間資訊科技服務及設備供應商、其他涉案公司的辦公室，以及涉案人士的住所。案情指有關供應商涉嫌圍標、合謀定價、瓜分市場及交換影響競爭的敏感資料，違反《競爭條例》下的第一行為守則。
競委會稱早前接獲投訴，指有供應商在提交虛擬實境系統報價時，為其他供應商及涉案公司準備標書，以作出掩護式投標。初步估計涉案合約總值約1000萬元。競委會指出，事件涉及學校及非牟利機構，懷疑反競爭行為有機會令選擇減少或成本上升，影響公共資源運用。
競委會暫未公布有人被起訴。調查仍在進行，會否交由競爭事務審裁處處理，仍有待進一步行動。
